sources.title: Mengjie Chen, Chao Gao and Zhao Ren, Robust Covariance and Scatter Matrix Estimation under Huber's Contamination Model
sources.locator: Full 53-page article and supplement retrieved. Read §3.1–§3.4, PDF pp.6–11 (matrix depth, Gaussian scaling, dense and block-sparse classes, Theorems 3.1–3.7); Theorem 7.1 and its proof, PDF pp.21–23; Theorem 5.1 and covariance lower-bound argument, PDF pp.46–47; and Lemma 7.3, PDF pp.50–51. The local slab-deviation argument is supplied independently. The lower-bound proof's sparse clean-rate citation is not adopted as a proof supplier; the assigned items contain a local packing obligation.

contents.name: §3.1, matrix depth definition, Gaussian scale beta and empirical estimator, Proposition 3.1
contents.reason: The empirical depth convention, including both weak inequalities and ties, is recorded. Degenerate Gaussian directions are handled with depth at least one half.

contents.name: Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, dense Huber covariance upper and lower risks
contents.reason: The planned regime and squared operator loss are retained. The lower proof's fixed-M qualification is recorded in batch notes.

contents.name: Theorems 3.6 and 3.7, single-block sparse Huber covariance upper and lower risks
contents.reason: The source's common-block support class and 2s-dimensional direction family are kept separate from weak-lq row sparsity.

contents.name: Theorem 7.1 and proof, bounded-class matrix-depth deviation under Huber contamination
contents.reason: The contamination-count and depth-comparison route is reproduced locally for every Borel positive-semidefinite statistic satisfying the empirical-depth comparison; the local measurable-selector lemma supplies this premise for global and bounded-class maximizers.

contents.name: Theorem 5.1 and covariance modulus calculation, PDF pp.46–47
contents.reason: The two-law contamination modulus route is used with an explicit fixed-M scaling.

contents.name: Lemma 7.3, PDF pp.50–51, slab-class VC and empirical-process argument
contents.reason: The proof is reconstructed from finite trace counting, symmetrization, chaining and bounded differences rather than importing the paper's cited inequalities.

contents.name: Gaussian covariance KL calculations used in the lower bounds
contents.reason: The local lemma derives the Gaussian densities from the stated normal convention and the change-of-variables supplier, then computes the quadratic expectation and trace formula; source lower-bound calculations are context, not a substitute proof.

contents.name: §5 two-point contamination reduction, extended to all matrix-valued actions
contents.reason: The local proof uses equalized Huber mixtures and the matrix triangle inequality for Borel actions in the full matrix space; the paper’s parameter-space action convention is not imported.

contents.name: §3.2, measurable matrix-depth maximizers
contents.reason: The source supplies the matrix-depth setting; the assigned item proves Borel selection locally by finite depth-level hit sets, lexicographic dyadic subdivision on compact classes, and a sample-dependent cap for global dense and single-block sparse classes.

sources.title: Stanislav Minsker and Xiaohan Wei, Estimation of the Covariance Structure of Heavy-Tailed Distributions
sources.locator: Full 21-page paper retrieved. Read estimator (2), robust mean pilot (3)–(4), fixed-scale Lemma 2.1 and adaptive Theorem 2.1, PDF pp.3–5; proof §§4.1–4.3, PDF pp.7–9; supplement Lemmas 5.1–5.7 and the uses of Lemma 5.5, PDF pp.12–20.

contents.name: Equations (1)–(6), median-of-means pilot, matrix truncation and finite scale grid
contents.reason: The scalar truncation is extended by spectral calculus and the pilot remains a separate robust-mean dependency.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 2.1, finite matrix-variance error bound
contents.reason: Complete corrected local proof now supplied: ambient p failure factor, broad trace-aware D sample condition, original same-sample pilot, uniform pilot-ball bound, known-mean oracle branch, and constants3/18. The original d-only sample condition is explicitly refuted by the new axis-family counterexample.

contents.name: Corollary 5.1, claimed inequality sigma0 squared at least tr(Sigma) times operator norm(Sigma)
contents.reason: This inequality is false for arbitrary distributions. The assigned B-page counterexample has Sigma=diag(1,1/2) and matrix variance diag(4/3,1), so 4/3 < 3/2.

contents.name: Lemma 5.7, matrix concentration for the truncated random matrices
contents.reason: The omitted source trace-MGF proof is not imported. Complete local finite-dimensional Golden–Thompson and bounded independent matrix Bernstein proofs now supply the concentration route, with clipping bias/variance and vector dilation computed locally.

contents.name: §2 finite matrix variance and intrinsic-dimension notation
contents.reason: The local fourth-moment argument proves the ratio is at least one from a top covariance eigenvector; no FKG claim is used.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1 and §4.3 adaptive scale comparison
contents.reason: The local helper retains the exact ceiling grid count and arbitrary-event transfer. Sharper per-scale concentration budgets plus one shared pilot event now prove the legitimate unrounded5p logarithmic bound; no false unrounded cardinality claim is used.

contents.name: Exact prescribed covariance pilot block budget
Known-mean covariance clipping and vector concentration without false trace comparison
Lemma 2.1 and §§4.1–4.2: fixed-scale truncated covariance deviation
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the same-sample pilot-ball perturbation bound and matrix concentration route, replacing the false d-only sample condition by the trace-aware D condition; no source trace comparison is imported.
